entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Henry Woodlock (died 1316), also known as Henry de Merewell, rose from Prior of Winchester Cathedral Priory to become Bishop of Winchester, serving from 1305 until his death. His episcopacy spanned the tumultuous reigns of King Edward I and Edward II, placing him at the heart of English ecclesiastical and political life during a period of significant transition. Woodlock's tenure as bishop was marked by his administrative competence, his involvement in major national and international church affairs, and his contributions to the ongoing architectural development of Winchester Cathedral, a pivotal institution in medieval England.

Elected Bishop on 23 October 1305, Woodlock received temporalities on 18 December 1305 and was consecrated on 30 January 1306 by Archbishop Robert Winchelsey at Canterbury. A highlight of his career was his active participation in the English proceedings against the Knights Templar, initiated in 1309, and his subsequent journey to the Council of Vienne (1311–1312). At Vienne, Pope Clement V formally dissolved the Order, a decision that profoundly impacted monastic and military orders across Europe. Within his diocese, Woodlock oversaw the administrative and spiritual welfare of one of England's wealthiest sees, managing its extensive estates and ensuring the continued functioning of its many parishes and religious houses.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Henry Woodlock's episcopacy was crucial for the stable governance of one of England's wealthiest dioceses during a period of national and ecclesiastical upheaval. His participation in the Council of Vienne directly contributed to the continent-wide dissolution of the Knights Templar, a major event in medieval European history.
